newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Long dollar sends South Korean won to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Long dollar sends South Korean won to higher close.

text.p: The South Korean won closed higher against the dollar on Thursday as banks and corporates unwound long dollar positions, traders said.
The won ended at an intraday high of 848.70, up from the opening rate of 849.00. It touched a low of 849.30.

"The dollar position seems relatively long and players feel that the Bank of Korea will step in if the dollar touches 850," said a foreign bank trader. The central bank has never acknowledged intervening in the interbank market.
But dealers said the won's trend was still weak on forecasts of a rising trade deficit and the impact of nationwide strikes.
Major export industries have been hit by the strikes in protest at the passage of a controversial labour law.
The trade minister said on Wednesday the strikes could make it difficult to control the snowballing trade deficit, which is forecast at $15 billion this year.
The dealer said he saw the won moving in a 848.50 to 849.50 range on Friday, while a local bank dealer put the range at 848 to 850.
